findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate datetime keys, so the audit-log endpoint fails on every non-empty page
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` is a copy of `Paginator.get_item_key`: it calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly on `getattr(item, self.key)`. The audit-log endpoint orders by `-datetime`, so the value is a `datetime` and `math.floor(datetime)` raises `TypeError`. `build_cursor` calls the key function on the first result, so any request with `optimized_pagination=true` that returns at least one row will 500. `value_from_cursor` (line 842) also returns the raw integer cursor value instead of converting the millisecond timestamp back to a `datetime` as `DateTimePaginator` does. Any follow-up cursor would therefore compare a datetime column against a raw integer. The new class should subclass or reuse `DateTimePaginator` semantics.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets are passed straight into queryset slicing, based on a false claim about the ORM
findings.body: The comment says the ORM "properly handles negative slicing automatically". It does not: Django querysets raise `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported` for a negative start or stop. Cursor offsets come from the user-supplied `cursor` query param (`Cursor.from_string` accepts any `int` for the offset, including negatives, with no validation). A request with `optimized_pagination=true` and a cursor like `0:-5:0` therefore reaches `queryset[start_offset:stop]` and returns a 500. The comments ("access to data beyond normal pagination bounds", "safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level") suggest the intent is to bypass pagination bounds. If negative indexing did work, it would let a caller read from the end of the dataset and sidestep the offset checks that other paginators enforce with `BadPaginationError`. The right fix is to reject negative offsets, not to enable them.

findings.title: Shared BasePaginator behaviour changed for all endpoints with a misleading comment and an inconsistent clamp
findings.body: This edit changes `BasePaginator.get_result`, which every endpoint using it shares, not just the audit-log endpoint. For forward cursors, a negative offset is now silently clamped to 0, where it used to fail loudly. That hides malformed or tampered cursors and can return a wrong page or loop. For `is_prev` cursors the negative offset is still passed through unchanged, so Django still raises on negative slicing, and the comment claiming negative offsets are now allowed and "safe" is false. The later check `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` also still uses the unclamped `offset`. Invalid offsets should be rejected explicitly, and this global change is unrelated to the PR's stated scope.

findings.title: organization_context.member can be None, causing AttributeError
findings.body: `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` dereferences `member` without a None check. For callers authenticated without an org membership (for example an API token or key with `org:write`, or a non-member user), `member` is `None`. Evaluating this line then raises `AttributeError` and returns a 500. The line runs on every request, even when `optimized_pagination` isn't set, so it can break the previously working default path. The `use_optimized` check should come first, and `member` should be guarded. The condition also reads as a security gate, but `has_global_access` is not a meaningful authorization check for an experimental pagination mode.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator.get_result wholesale
findings.body: The new class copies about 70 lines of `BasePaginator.get_result`. The only differences are the negative-offset branch and a duplicated `start_offset` branch that is identical to the base behaviour. Any future fix to the base cursor logic must now be applied twice, and the two copies will drift. The "optimized query path" described in the docstring does not exist: there is no query optimization, just a different slicing path. The code should be an override of the one differing step or should not exist.

findings.title: Comment claims negative offsets are supported but nothing validates or implements this
findings.body: The added comment says negative offsets are allowed for "efficient reverse pagination", but no code changed. `Cursor` accepts any integer offset, and nothing downstream (Django slicing) supports negative values. The comment misleads maintainers into thinking negative offsets are a supported feature of the cursor contract. It also lets unvalidated user input flow into the paginators. The comment should be removed, or `Cursor` should validate non-negative offsets.

findings.title: No tests for the new paginator, the optimized_pagination flag, or negative-offset handling
findings.body: The PR adds a new paginator class, a new query parameter with a permission-dependent code path, changes to the shared `BasePaginator` slicing, and negative-offset cursor handling, but includes no tests. A single test that hit the endpoint with `optimized_pagination=true` would have exposed the `TypeError` on datetime keys. Tests are also needed for admin versus non-admin gating, negative cursor offsets, and prev/next cursor round-trips. The description is also just 'Test 1' and gives no rationale or benchmark for the claimed performance gains.
